newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end weak on liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end weak on liquidation.

text.p: Liquidation of key index stocks sent the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) to close lower on Friday, dealers said. After trading to a high of 2,086.72, the index ended 15.06 points lower at 2,068.17.
Cycle & Carriage and Singapore Press Holdings contributed to the bulk of the weakness.

"There was a fair bit of liquidation of key property counters like DBS Land, CityDev and Straits Steamship Land," a dealer with a European institution said. "There was also a significant amount of continued selling of SIA on recent recommendations to reduce exposure," he said.

He added investors sold SPH ahead of its results. After the market closed, SPH reported its profit for the year ended August 31 fell 1.1 percent to Singapore $307.63 million (US$218.18 million). Market turnover was at 108.8 million shares, with losers leading gainers by 162 to 137.

Labroy Marine, which ended at S$1.19, led the actives with 6.1 million shares. Malaysian Ho Wah Genting was also among the actives with 4.6 million shares. It rose S$0.41 to S$1.36 on rumours that it was a take-over target. Company officials declined comment.
OCBC Foreign and CityDev led losers, shedding S$0.50 and S$0.40 to S$15.60 and S$10.70 respectively.
